http/cookie_jar#

Cookie jars: where a client keeps cookies between requests.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

let jar = MemoryCookieJar();
let client = HttpClient(cookies: jar);
SavedCookieJar(origin: jar, destination: file).file();          // save
let restored = LoadedCookieJar(origin: file, clock: SystemClock()).jar();

Description#

Cookie jars: where a client keeps cookies between requests.

A MemoryCookieJar holds at most 3000 cookies and 180 per domain by default; beyond that it evicts, non-secure cookies first. Session cookies and expired ones are not saved.

object MemoryCookieJar#

object MemoryCookieJar does CookieStoring, Closing

The only mutable capability is an explicit Atomic cell of immutable records. Each HTTP call publishes once, with no suspension or caller callbacks between reading the cell and publication. The clock is observed before the state read.

object SavedCookieJar#

object SavedCookieJar

Explicit filesystem commands; construction performs no I/O. The intermediate file is closed before same-directory rename, with deferred private-directory cleanup on failure. Atomic visibility does not promise power-loss durability.
